description: An introduction to foreign trade covering imports, exports, re-exports, visible and invisible trade, the balance of trade and balance of payments, trade documents, barriers and terms of trade at Form 1 level.

mcq.questionText: Foreign trade is best defined as the buying and selling of goods and services between:

options.text: A retailer and a final consumer

mcq.explanation: Foreign or international trade takes place across national borders, between people or businesses in different countries.

mcq.questionText: Goods that a country buys from other countries are called:
mcq.explanation: Imports are goods purchased from foreign countries and brought into the home country.

mcq.questionText: When Tanzania sells coffee to Germany, this coffee is an example of:
mcq.explanation: Exports are goods produced in the home country and sold to other countries.

mcq.questionText: Goods that are imported into a country and then sold again to another country without major change are known as:
mcq.explanation: Re-exports are goods first imported and later exported again to another country, often after storage or repackaging.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of invisible trade?

options.text: Earning money from foreign tourists visiting Tanzania

mcq.explanation: Invisible trade involves services such as tourism, banking, insurance and transport rather than physical goods.

mcq.questionText: Trade in physical goods that can be seen and touched is called:
mcq.explanation: Visible trade is trade in tangible goods such as crops, minerals and manufactured products.

mcq.questionText: The difference between the value of a country's visible exports and visible imports is called the:
mcq.explanation: The balance of trade compares only the value of visible exports against visible imports.

mcq.questionText: A country has a favourable balance of trade when:

options.text: Visible imports are greater than visible exports
Visible exports are greater than visible imports
It only trades within its borders

mcq.explanation: A favourable (surplus) balance of trade occurs when the value of visible exports exceeds the value of visible imports.

mcq.questionText: The balance of payments differs from the balance of trade because it records:

options.text: Both visible and invisible transactions with other countries

mcq.explanation: The balance of payments is a wider record of all transactions, both visible and invisible, between a country and the rest of the world.

mcq.questionText: Which one of these is a common reason why countries engage in foreign trade?

options.text: To obtain goods they cannot produce themselves
To reduce the number of traders

mcq.explanation: No country produces everything it needs, so foreign trade lets countries obtain goods and resources they lack.

mcq.questionText: A tax charged on imported goods is called a:
mcq.explanation: A tariff is a customs duty placed on imports, often to raise revenue or protect local industries.

mcq.questionText: A limit set on the quantity of a particular good that may be imported is known as a:
mcq.explanation: A quota restricts the amount or volume of goods that can be imported during a given period.

mcq.questionText: Which document is sent by the exporter to the importer showing the goods supplied and the amount owed?
mcq.explanation: The commercial invoice lists the goods, their prices and the total amount the importer must pay.

mcq.questionText: One disadvantage of foreign trade to a developing country is that it may:

options.text: Widen the variety of goods available
Lead to over-dependence on other countries

mcq.explanation: Relying heavily on imports or on a few export markets can make a country too dependent on others.

mcq.questionText: Terms of trade refers to the relationship between:

options.text: The prices of a country's exports and the prices of its imports
The number of traders and customers

mcq.explanation: Terms of trade compare export prices with import prices; they improve when export prices rise relative to import prices.

fib.questionText: Trade carried out between people in different countries is known as _____ trade.
fib.explanation: Foreign trade, also called international trade, crosses national borders.

fib.questionText: Goods bought from other countries and brought into the home country are called _____.
fib.explanation: Imports flow into a country from abroad.

fib.questionText: Goods produced locally and sold to other countries are called _____.
fib.explanation: Exports leave the home country to be sold abroad.

fib.questionText: Goods that are imported and then sold again to another country are called _____.
fib.explanation: Re-exports are goods imported first and then exported to a third country.

fib.questionText: Trade in services such as banking, insurance and tourism is called _____ trade.
fib.explanation: Invisible trade deals with services rather than physical goods.

fib.questionText: The difference between the value of visible exports and visible imports is called the balance of _____.
fib.explanation: The balance of trade considers only visible goods.

fib.questionText: A record of all visible and invisible transactions between one country and the rest of the world is called the balance of _____.
fib.explanation: The balance of payments is wider than the balance of trade.

fib.questionText: A tax placed on imported goods is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Tariffs raise revenue and can protect local producers.

fib.questionText: A document that lists the goods supplied and the amount the importer must pay is the commercial _____.
fib.explanation: The invoice shows goods, prices and the total due.

fib.questionText: The relationship between the prices of a country's exports and the prices of its imports is called the _____ of trade.
fib.explanation: Terms of trade improve when export prices rise relative to import prices.

tf.questionText: Foreign trade takes place between people living in different countries.
tf.explanation: Foreign trade crosses national borders, unlike home trade.

tf.questionText: Imports are goods that a country sells to other countries.
tf.explanation: Imports are bought from abroad; goods sold to other countries are exports.

tf.questionText: Tourism earnings from foreign visitors are an example of invisible trade.
tf.explanation: Tourism is a service, so it is counted as invisible trade.

tf.questionText: Visible trade involves buying and selling of physical goods.
tf.explanation: Visible trade deals with tangible goods that can be seen.

tf.questionText: The balance of trade includes both visible and invisible transactions.
tf.explanation: The balance of trade covers only visible goods; the balance of payments covers both.

tf.questionText: A country has an unfavourable balance of trade when its visible imports exceed its visible exports.
tf.explanation: When imports are greater than exports, the balance of trade is unfavourable (a deficit).

tf.questionText: A quota is a tax charged on every imported good.
tf.explanation: A quota limits the quantity of goods imported; a tax on imports is a tariff.

tf.questionText: Foreign trade allows countries to obtain goods they cannot produce themselves.
tf.explanation: One main reason for foreign trade is to acquire goods and resources a country lacks.

tf.questionText: Re-exports are goods that are produced locally and sold abroad for the first time.
tf.explanation: Re-exports are first imported and then exported again, not locally produced goods.

tf.questionText: A country's terms of trade improve when the prices of its exports rise compared with the prices of its imports.
tf.explanation: Higher export prices relative to import prices mean better terms of trade.

summary.correctAnswer: Buying and selling of goods and services between different countries.
summary.explanation: Also called international trade; it crosses national borders.

summary.correctAnswer: Goods and services bought from other countries.
summary.explanation: They flow into the home country from abroad.

summary.correctAnswer: Goods and services sold to other countries.
summary.explanation: They earn foreign exchange for the home country.

summary.correctAnswer: Goods first imported and then sold again to another country.
summary.explanation: Often stored or repackaged before being exported again.

summary.correctAnswer: Visible trade is in physical goods; invisible trade is in services.
summary.explanation: Examples: goods like coffee (visible); tourism and insurance (invisible).

summary.correctAnswer: Difference between the value of visible exports and visible imports.
Record of all visible and invisible transactions with other countries.
summary.explanation: Wider than the balance of trade.

summary.correctAnswer: To obtain goods not produced locally and to sell surplus production.
summary.explanation: It also earns foreign exchange and widens the market.

summary.correctAnswer: Tariffs (taxes on imports) and quotas (limits on quantities imported).
summary.explanation: Used to raise revenue or protect local industries.

summary.correctAnswer: Relationship between the prices of a country's exports and its imports.
summary.explanation: They improve when export prices rise relative to import prices.

hoq.questionText: A country imports cars and machinery worth 800 billion shillings and exports crops and minerals worth 500 billion shillings in one year. What can be said about its balance of trade?

options.text: It has a favourable balance of trade
It has an unfavourable balance of trade
Its balance of trade is exactly equal
It has no balance of trade at all

hoq.explanation: Because visible imports (800 billion) exceed visible exports (500 billion), the balance of trade is unfavourable, showing a deficit.

hoq.questionText: Why might a government decide to place high tariffs on imported sugar even though this raises the price for local consumers?

options.text: To encourage people to stop buying sugar completely
To protect local sugar producers from cheap foreign competition
To increase the amount of sugar imported

hoq.explanation: High tariffs make imported sugar more expensive, helping local producers compete and survive, even though consumers pay more.

hoq.questionText: A country's visible imports are greater than its visible exports, yet its overall balance of payments is favourable. What best explains this?

options.text: It earns large amounts from invisible exports such as tourism and shipping
It has stopped all foreign trade

hoq.explanation: The balance of payments includes invisible trade, so strong earnings from services like tourism can offset a deficit in visible goods.
